title: M4, NGC 6121
caption: The globular cluster M4, imaged by the KPNO 0.9-meter telescope

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This picture shows M4, also cataloged as NGC 6121, a globular cluster in the constellation Scorpius. It has a slightly brownish color, and an unusual bar-like structure runs through its center.

M4 lies about 7000 light-years away, which makes it a good candidate for the nearest globular cluster to us. It would look much brighter if not for a considerable amount of interstellar dust between us and the cluster. That same dust is responsible for its brownish tint.

Dust between the stars absorbs and scatters light, and it affects blue light more strongly than red, so objects seen through it look dimmer and redder than they really are. A globular cluster is a dense, roughly spherical swarm of old stars bound together by gravity. Being so close, M4 is a convenient place to study the individual stars of such a cluster.
scale: M4 is about 7000 light-years away, according to NOIRLab.

understand.summary: The T2KA CCD camera on the Kitt Peak 0.9-meter telescope recorded M4 in visible light. The filters and color mapping are not published.
understand.eye: The camera's exposures gather far more light than the eye and resolve many of the cluster's individual stars.
